title: Marinating
steps: Mix salt, acid, oil, and aromatics until evenly combined.
Coat food on all sides in a shallow dish or bag.
Refrigerate 30 minutes to overnight, depending on thickness.
Pat food dry before high-heat cooking for better browning.
tip: Do not over-marinate in strong acid; it can make surfaces mushy, so keep fish and thin cuts brief.
watch_query: how to marinate meat properly short video

title: Making a spice paste
steps: Toast dry spices briefly until fragrant, if using whole spices.
Add spices, aromatics, salt, and a little liquid or oil.
Grind or blend until mostly smooth, scraping sides once or twice.
Cook paste in oil until darker, glossy, and fragrant.
tip: Avoid adding too much water at first; a loose paste splatters and takes longer to fry off.
watch_query: how to make spice paste cooking video

title: Blooming whole spices (tadka)
steps: Heat oil or ghee in a small pan until shimmering.
Add whole spices and stand back from popping seeds.
Cook until sizzling, fragrant, and slightly darker, 10–60 seconds.
Pour immediately over the dish or add aromatics to stop cooking.
tip: Do not burn the spices; have the next ingredient ready before they hit the hot oil.
watch_query: how to temper spices tadka short video

title: Searing
steps: Pat food very dry and season just before cooking.
Heat a heavy pan until oil shimmers and moves easily.
Lay food away from you; leave it still until browned.
Turn when it releases easily and sear the next side.
tip: Crowding the pan traps steam, so cook in batches with space between pieces.
watch_query: how to sear meat in a pan short video

title: Pan-frying
steps: Add enough oil to cover the pan bottom generously.
Heat until a breadcrumb sizzles on contact.
Lower food in away from you, without crowding.
Flip when edges brown; drain on a rack or paper.
tip: If the oil is too cool, food absorbs grease; wait for a steady sizzle before adding more.
watch_query: how to pan fry cutlets short video

title: Stir-frying
steps: Cut everything small and uniform before heating the pan.
Heat wok or skillet until oil shimmers and just smokes.
Add ingredients in batches, tossing constantly over high heat.
Add sauce near the end; cook until glossy and reduced.
tip: Do not start before prep is complete; stir-frying moves too fast for chopping mid-cook.
watch_query: basic stir fry technique short video

title: Deep-frying
steps: Fill a deep pot less than halfway with oil.
Heat to 350–375°F, or until batter sizzles immediately.
Lower food gently with tongs or a spider.
Fry until golden and crisp; drain on a rack.
tip: Never overcrowd or overfill the pot; hot oil can foam up and spill dangerously.
watch_query: how to deep fry safely at home video

title: Roasting
steps: Heat the oven fully before adding food.
Coat food lightly with oil, salt, and seasonings.
Spread in one layer on a hot or sturdy pan.
Roast until browned outside and tender inside, turning if needed.
tip: Too much food on the tray causes steaming, so leave gaps for dry heat to circulate.
watch_query: how to roast vegetables properly short video

title: Grilling
steps: Preheat grates until very hot, then clean and oil them.
Pat food dry and season before placing on the grill.
Cook over direct heat for char; move to indirect heat to finish.
Rest meat before slicing so juices settle.
tip: Do not force food off the grate; wait until grill marks form and it releases easily.
watch_query: basic grilling technique direct indirect heat video

title: Braising
steps: Brown the main ingredient well in a heavy pot.
Cook aromatics until softened and fragrant.
Add liquid halfway up the food, scraping browned bits.
Cover and cook gently until fork-tender.
tip: Do not boil hard; a quiet simmer keeps meat moist and prevents tough, stringy texture.
watch_query: how to braise meat basic technique video

title: Simmering
steps: Bring liquid just to a boil first, if needed.
Reduce heat until small bubbles rise gently.
Skim foam or fat from the surface when necessary.
Cook uncovered or covered as the recipe requires.
tip: A simmer is not a rolling boil; lower the heat when bubbles become large and constant.
watch_query: simmer vs boil cooking technique video

title: Steaming
steps: Add water below the steamer basket, not touching food.
Bring water to a steady boil before adding food.
Cover tightly; open lid away from your face.
Steam until tender, checking water level if cooking long.
tip: Steam burns fast; lift lids away from you and keep hands clear of escaping vapor.
watch_query: how to steam vegetables with steamer basket video

title: Boiling
steps: Use enough water for food to move freely.
Salt the water if cooking pasta, grains, or vegetables.
Bring to large, rolling bubbles over high heat.
Add food and adjust heat to maintain boiling.
tip: Adding food drops the temperature, so let the water return to a boil before timing closely.
watch_query: how to boil pasta properly short video

title: Baking
steps: Preheat the oven fully and position racks as needed.
Measure ingredients accurately, especially flour and leavening.
Use the specified pan size and prepare it properly.
Bake until set, browned, or a tester comes out clean.
tip: Opening the oven often drops heat, so check only near the suggested doneness time.
watch_query: basic baking techniques for beginners video

title: Cooking rice in stock
steps: Rinse rice until water runs mostly clear, if using long-grain rice.
Combine rice, stock, and salt; adjust salt for salty stock.
Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Rest covered 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
tip: Do not add full salt before tasting the stock; reduced stock can make rice too salty.
watch_query: how to cook rice in chicken stock video

title: Cooking plain rice
steps: Rinse rice until the water is mostly clear.
Add rice and measured water to a tight-lidded pot.
Bring to a boil, cover, and turn heat to low.
Cook until water is absorbed; rest covered 10 minutes.
tip: Do not lift the lid during cooking; trapped steam is what finishes the grains evenly.
watch_query: how to cook plain white rice on stove video

title: Layering and slow-steaming (dum)
steps: Part-cook rice until grains are firm but no longer raw.
Layer rice with cooked masala, herbs, and fat in a heavy pot.
Seal the lid with dough or foil to trap steam.
Cook on very low heat until fragrant and fully steamed.
tip: High heat scorches the bottom before the center steams, so use a heavy pot and low flame.

title: Scrambling eggs
steps: Beat eggs with salt until yolks and whites are fully mixed.
Melt butter or heat oil over medium-low heat.
Add eggs and stir slowly with a spatula.
Remove when softly set; residual heat finishes them.
tip: Do not cook over high heat; eggs turn dry and rubbery before you can stop them.
watch_query: how to scramble eggs soft curds video

title: Kneading dough
steps: Mix flour and liquid until no dry patches remain.
Press dough away with your palm, then fold it back.
Rotate and repeat until smoother and elastic.
Rest dough if it resists stretching or tears quickly.
tip: Avoid adding lots of flour while kneading; sticky dough often smooths out with time and motion.
watch_query: how to knead dough by hand video

title: Wrapping and rolling
steps: Place filling slightly off-center on the wrapper or dough.
Fold the near edge over filling and tuck snugly.
Fold in sides to seal the ends, if needed.
Roll firmly without squeezing filling out; seal the edge.
tip: Overfilling causes tears and leaks, so use less filling until your rolls close easily.
watch_query: how to wrap and roll spring rolls video

title: Poaching
steps: Heat seasoned liquid until barely steaming, not boiling.
Add delicate food gently, keeping it fully submerged.
Cook at 160–180°F with only tiny bubbles.
Remove when just cooked and still tender.
tip: Boiling is too rough for poaching; keep the liquid quiet to avoid tough or broken food.
watch_query: how to poach fish or eggs technique video

title: Blending a sauce smooth
steps: Cool hot sauce slightly before blending.
Fill blender no more than halfway with hot liquid.
Vent the lid and cover with a towel while blending.
Blend until smooth, then adjust thickness and seasoning.
tip: Hot liquid expands in a sealed blender, so vent the lid to prevent dangerous splashes.
